scope: single controlled fixed path; no PlayWorld score or SOTA claim

memory.method: bounded early-view pose KV retrieval; diagnostic, not paper reproduction
memory.pose_source: commanded poses, not reconstructed realized poses
memory.key_storage: canonical pre-RoPE BF16 keys; reapply spatial and virtual temporal RoPE on read

caveat: Commanded camera closure does not prove realized closure. Endpoint image similarity cannot establish world memory if the realized route fails.

visual_judge.prompt: Evaluate two anonymized world-model videos independently and then compare. Each was given the same image and fixed camera path. Commands by one-second chunk: ['WAIT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'WAIT']. RIGHT and LEFT yaw 60 degrees per second; W moves forward. Commands are NOT proof that motion happened. Inspect actual frames. Assess whether each video realizes a turnaround and return to the starting viewpoint; whether persistent landmark identity, any sign text, geometry and spatial layout match on return; and whether there are sudden jumps, frozen motion or implausible transitions. Distinguish camera-control failures from forgetting. Do not reward a similar final building if reaching it required a reset. Do not invent unseen geometry. Return English JSON with keys A and B (each with realized_round_trip: yes|no|uncertain, starting_place_recovered: yes|no|uncertain, discontinuity: yes|no|uncertain, visual_evidence, failure_classification), preference: A|B|tie|neither, confidence: low|medium|high, and reasoning. This is a diagnostic comparison, not a benchmark score.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 hold the initial Primemall view (angular dark roof, diamond-patterned terracotta facade, 'Primemall' sign), matching the WAIT chunk. From about frame 10 the view pans steadily right. Primemall exits left, the 'Diemell' terracotta block with a large blue umbrella enters, and the view reaches a glass-fronted plaza building with a railing and paved courtyard around frames 35-45. The pan then reverses: the glass building recedes, the 'Diemell' block and umbrella return around frames 45-58, and Primemall re-enters from the left around frames 58-62. It settles on Primemall for frames 65-78. Landmarks return in consistent order and relative layout. The Primemall sign text, twin peaked roof and facade pattern are preserved on return. The final framing is not pixel-identical to the start. A blue umbrella and patio furniture now sit in the left foreground, and the building appears slightly offset and closer. This is consistent with a small viewpoint drift, or with foreground elements seen during the pan, rather than a reset. The transitions are gradual with no cuts or freezes beyond the commanded WAIT segments.
A.failure_classification: Minor camera-control imprecision: the final framing is slightly offset and the visible yaw is less than a clean 180 degrees. There is no evident forgetting, because landmark identity, sign text and layout are retained on return.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-48 essentially match A: a hold on Primemall, a right pan past 'Diemell' to the glass plaza building, then the start of a left return. Around frames 49-52 the returning 'Diemell' facade morphs. The sign reads 'Diremall' and then 'Pirtemall'/'Pitemall', with a ghosted 'Prime...' sign beneath it on the same terracotta block. This fuses Diemell and Primemall into a hybrid structure. Instead of settling on the original Primemall view, the camera keeps panning left. From about frame 60 onward it reaches a different building with a darker brown facade, an illegible 'Dinno'/'Prientgrall' sign and a large white umbrella. The lighting shifts to a dimmer, overcast or dusk tone. The final frames (65-78) hold on this new building, which never appeared in the starting view. Primemall's original front-on view is never recovered.
B.failure_classification: Forgetting/hallucination: landmarks blend during the return (duplicated, morphing sign text), and a new building and lighting condition replace the start scene. This is compounded by a likely camera-control overshoot or yaw drift during the LEFT chunks. The changes in identity and lighting go beyond what a pure rotation error would produce.

result.reasoning: Both videos share a nearly identical outbound path, so the difference lies entirely in the return. A smoothly reverses through the same landmarks in the correct order. It ends on a recognizable Primemall with consistent sign text and geometry, with only a modest framing offset and some added foreground patio elements. B corrupts landmark identity during the return through a merged Diemell/Primemall facade with garbled, duplicated signage. It then overshoots into a newly invented building under different lighting and never revisits the starting viewpoint. A's flaw is minor camera imprecision, while B's is substantive memory failure plus probable camera overshoot.
